headline: Audits catch leaky benchmarks, inflated AUCs and age gaps in ECG AI
subtitle: A week of meta-research shows reported performance often outruns what models deliver
tldr: Preprint audits found AUCs clustering at round thresholds, patient leakage in MIMIC-CXR benchmarks, and AQ-10 label circularity inflating autism-screening accuracy.
Four ECG foundation models, probed on 5.4 million ECGs, performed worse in older adults. The preprint traces the gap to the data, not the models.
In a 368-person phase 3 RCT, AI diabetes-prevention coaching drew faster, steadier engagement, but participants rated human coaching higher.

paper_themes.summary: Re-audits show leakage, circular labels and threshold-chasing inflate reported performance. Externally validated IVF models pooled lower, though not significantly, and neurosurgery AUCs were extremely heterogeneous.

paper_themes.theme: Moving models across sites and populations
paper_themes.summary: ECG foundation models lost accuracy with age, and uncertainty missed post-transfer performance loss. An AD MRI classifier trained on Western data held up in a Chinese cohort.

paper_themes.theme: Testing AI with people and workflows
paper_themes.summary: An RCT found AI coaching traded satisfaction for engagement. AI cut breast-biopsy review time 43.5% in a retrospective study. Teen-chatbot safety failures persisted despite teen-aware prompting.

top_papers.note: Rare phase 3 RCT of patient-facing AI: faster uptake and engagement, but lower satisfaction than human coaching.
Preprint covering 13 cohorts: age, not sex or race, drives the largest worst-group gap across ECG foundation models.
Preprint covering 2,001 Q1-journal articles: metrics cluster at round numbers, and about one in eight ROC curves mismatch the reported AUC.
Patient-separated evaluation on MIMIC-CXR erased apparent gains; a label lookup table nearly matched the best model.
Preprint: after transfer from MIMIC-IV to eICU, uncertainty helped defer false alarms but missed the performance drop and most deaths.

grants_summary: A thin week for AI funding. Three VA awards apply random forests, reinforcement learning and personalized risk to fatty liver disease (NAFLD), CKD mineral-bone disorder and lung screening. NSF awards are general methods work.

top_grants.note: Adds dynamic random-forest risk models to a working VA NAFLD dashboard to cut unnecessary referrals.
Combines a validated systems-biology model with reinforcement learning to personalize CKD mineral-bone disorder treatment for veterans.
Targets veterans missed by USPSTF criteria, including those with military exposures; pairs with this week's Sybil safety-net preprint.

products_summary: Two cardiovascular software 510(k) clearances, with no performance details in the records. Industry news paired Claude-assisted CAR-T engineering and an AI clinical-data funding round with STAT skepticism after heart-drug failures.

top_products.note: Cardiovascular software cleared under code DPS; no subgroup data in the record, which matters given this week's ECG age findings.
Generate Biomedicines says it used Anthropic's Claude to shrink CAR-T cell engines; a company claim, not published data.
STAT argues recent heart-drug failures should temper claims that AI speeds up drug research.

research_gaps.gap: Unknown how well deployed ECG AI performs in adults aged 75+
research_gaps.evidence: Preprint: 30-day MACE AUROC was 0.64-0.71 at age 75+ versus 0.81-0.90 under 40. This week's cardiovascular 510(k) records report no age-group results.
research_gaps.suggested_study: Age-stratified external validation of cleared ECG algorithms in older-adult cohorts, with post-market subgroup reporting and recalibration targets.

research_gaps.gap: No real-time warning, before outcomes are known, of AI performance loss after transfer
research_gaps.evidence: After transfer to eICU, AUROC fell to 0.76-0.77. No uncertainty measure flagged the loss, and missed deaths carried low uncertainty.
research_gaps.suggested_study: Prospective multi-site study comparing uncertainty, input-drift and rapid outcome-label audits for detecting degradation of transferred mortality models.

research_gaps.gap: Public clinical benchmarks lack patient-level split and label-provenance audits
research_gaps.evidence: Record-level MIMIC-CXR splits and AQ-10 labels built from the input items inflated accuracy. Q1-journal AUCs cluster at round thresholds.
research_gaps.suggested_study: Re-audit the most-cited public clinical datasets for leakage and circular labels, then publish corrected splits and re-scored leaderboards.

social.linkedin_post:
This week's BioMed AI Watch is about whether reported performance holds up.

• A meta-research preprint covering 2,001 prediction-model articles in top-quartile journals found AUC, sensitivity and specificity clustering at round numbers. About 1 in 8 ROC curves did not match the reported AUC.
• An audit of a MIMIC-CXR benchmark found that its apparent gains disappeared once patients were kept separate between training and test sets.
• A preprint testing four ECG foundation models on 5.4 million ECGs found performance fell with age. It traces the gap to the data, not the models.
• After moving from one hospital system's data to another's, uncertainty scores did not warn of a mortality model's performance drop (preprint).

On the trial side, a 368-person phase 3 RCT found an AI diabetes-prevention program got people started sooner and kept engagement steadier. Participants still rated human coaching higher.

Most findings above are preprints and not yet peer-reviewed. The common lesson is that patient-level splits, subgroup reporting and post-deployment monitoring belong in the evaluation itself.
